title: C2280G — Body Control Module (BCM)
introduction:
I use this reference as a seating chart for the body control module’s connections: the drawing locates a cavity, and the assignment table tells us which circuit belongs there. The BCM coordinates body electrical functions; this connector’s entries include lighting, the electrical steering-column lock, diagnostic CAN connections and fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies. Plenty of different conversations share this housing, so neighboring cavities need not have neighboring jobs.

Start with the connector identification table, then match a cavity label in the drawing to the Cavity column. Read across that same row for its circuit identifier, color, gauge, function and terminal part number. Where a cavity has repeated entries, keep those entries separate: different gauge and terminal combinations are recorded without a qualifier explaining which applies to a particular vehicle.

This is a connector-reading reference. Physical viewing direction, access, disconnection, probing, electrical test conditions and replacement methods are outside its scope. Gauge conventions and the metadata codes are not defined here, so I retain them without turning them into wire-selection advice. The overall pin-count entry also disagrees with the illustrated cavity range; that discrepancy remains open.

edits.why: I navigate the drawing by its printed cavity labels. Across the upper rows, the labels descend from left to right; farther down, the spacing changes around the long central housing feature. Continuing an imagined grid through that area would put the reader in the wrong seat. Gray-filled positions correspond here to table entries without assigned circuits. The outer projections provide visual landmarks, but their release or locking functions are not identified, and the drawing does not establish the physical viewing direction.

The cavity label connects the drawing to the table; the circuit identifier and Function entry explain the connection’s recorded job. Keep the lighting distinctions intact, including left versus right, high versus low beam, and front-right-or-common versus front-left fog lamps. The park-lamp relay entry identifies a circuit function, not necessarily a separate plug-in relay. Preserve the steering-column-lock positive designation, the separate high-speed CAN high and low labels, and every fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative. Read repeated cavity entries independently rather than combining their gauges or terminal parts. Blank Qualifier cells do not resolve applicability, and the Used field alone is not a test result. After identifying an entry, any electrical check needs its own matching diagnostic instructions.

originalAuthorHold: The identification table gives Pin Count as 26, while the illustration and assignment table cover cavities 1–22. Confirm the intended pin count or whether additional cavity information is missing; do not invent extra positions.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 47 primary units, three complete source pages and sole figure, and 2 edits. Count and repeated gauge/terminal applicability ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
